title: Albstadt and Sigmaringen
description: Two small towns in the hills of Baden-Württemberg, one university of applied sciences and a region with a strong technical industry.
html:
Two campuses in the Swabian hills

Albstadt and Sigmaringen lie about 30 kilometres apart in the south of Baden-Württemberg, on the edge of the Swabian Alb. The landscape is what people notice first: wooded hills, the young Danube and, in Sigmaringen, a castle above the river. The towns are small, with a combined population of around 60,000, and daily life is calm and affordable compared with the state's big cities.

Studying and working here

The two towns share a university of applied sciences with a technical profile: engineering, computer science, textile technology and business are its strongest areas, and several master's programmes are taught in English. Small class sizes and close contact with the regional industry are the main selling points. The region has a long history in textiles and precision engineering, and many graduates find their first job with one of the mid-sized manufacturers nearby. Stuttgart is about an hour and a half away by car for weekends in a bigger city.
